title: PARLIAMENT QUESTIONS: Access to Higher Education under National Digital University Initiative
body_text:
The Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with a  vision to strengthen learner-centric and technology-enabled education. In alignment with this vision, the Government has envisaged the establishment of a Digital University platform to provide flexible learning for all students.
The National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of  Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), launched the “NIELIT Digital University (NDU)  Platform” in October 2025 to facilitate access to digital learning opportunities for learners, including those from rural, remote and tribal areas. The NDU provides online and blended, skill-based courses in emerging technology areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud computing,  Industry 4.0 and other frontier domains.
The NDU Platform has reached learners from more than 750 districts in the country, with over 2.70  lakh registrations, and currently offers more than 100 courses across various disciplines. The Platform also provides learners an option to register on the NIELIT Alumni-cum-Placement Portal, enabling  them to access employment opportunities and mentoring facilities. Since October 2025, more  than 35,000 learners and more than 190 recruiters have registered on the Alumni Portal.
Additionally, in alignment with the objectives of NEP 2020, the Ministry of Education is implementing the National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT) Scheme. The Scheme promotes the use of technology in all processes of education.
To strengthen industry-academia linkages and enhance employability of learners, SWAYAM Plus platform has been launched under NMEICT scheme. The Platform offers more than 500 employability-focused courses. These courses have been curated from more than 80 industry partners across 15 sectors, including information technology, artificial intelligence, semiconductor  manufacturing, and advanced manufacturing etc. So far, more than 6 lakh learners have enrolled on  SWAYAM Plus platform for their skill augmentation.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar detailed progress under the National Digital University Initiative, aligned with NEP 2020. The NIELIT Digital University (NDU) Platform, launched in October 2025 by MeitY's NIELIT, has reached learners in over 750 districts with more than 2.70 lakh registrations and offers 100+ courses in emerging tech areas. Additionally, the SWAYAM Plus platform under the NMEICT scheme offers 500+ employability-focused courses curated from 80+ industry partners across 15 sectors, with over 6 lakh enrollments.
enrichment.context:
The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 emphasizes technology-enabled, flexible, and multidisciplinary learning to widen access to higher education, particularly for underserved populations in rural, remote, and tribal areas. The NDU Platform and SWAYAM Plus are concrete implementations of this vision, seeking to bridge the digital divide and align academic learning with industry needs through skill-based, employability-focused courses in frontier technologies like AI, cybersecurity, and semiconductor manufacturing. These platforms build on earlier digital education initiatives such as SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) and the broader NMEICT scheme, which has been operational since the 12th Five Year Plan period to mainstream ICT in education across India.

The inclusion of an Alumni-cum-Placement Portal reflects a growing policy focus on linking education outcomes to employability, addressing long-standing concerns about the mismatch between academic credentials and job-market skills in India. Such initiatives are significant for India's demographic dividend, as they aim to reskill and upskill a large youth population in emerging technology domains critical to the digital economy, Industry 4.0, and India's aspirations in sectors like semiconductor manufacturing under initiatives such as the India Semiconductor Mission.

prelims_questions.question: The 'NIELIT Digital University (NDU) Platform' mentioned in the context of India's higher education digital initiatives is administered under which Ministry?
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
prelims_questions.explanation: The NDU Platform was launched by NIELIT, which functions under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), even though it aligns with NEP 2020 objectives overseen by the Ministry of Education.

prelims_questions.question: The SWAYAM Plus platform, aimed at enhancing industry-academia linkages, has been launched under which scheme?
options: National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT)
prelims_questions.explanation: SWAYAM Plus has been launched under the NMEICT scheme implemented by the Ministry of Education, which promotes the use of technology across education processes as per NEP 2020.
